newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak BSE posts record volume SKK17.1bln in Feb.
newsitem.headline: Slovak BSE posts record volume SKK17.1bln in Feb.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Thursday said total turnover, influenced heavily by off-floor trading, reached a record volume of 17.1 billion crowns in February, up from 10.5 billion in January.

The BSE said in a statement that direct trades accounted for 16.3 billion crowns of the total, up from January's 10.25 billion crowns. Average daily turnover in February was 856.6 million crowns, it added.
Stockbrokers said the large proportion of direct trades reflected the market's low liquidity and lack of transparency.

"Too much is done through direct trades and the market remains illiquid and untransparent since direct deal prices often fail to reflect the real market value of a share," Bohus Betko of ING Barings told Reuters.

Trading involving listed blue chips totalled 6.0 billion crowns, with steel maker VSZ and commercial bank VUB leading in terms of volume, with trades totalling 116.5 million crowns and 91.7 million, respectively.
Trading of unlisted stocks reached a volume of 4.0 billion crowns, of which direct trades accounted for 3.9 billion.
Deals with bonds accounted for 41 percent of the entire turnover, totalling 7.1 billion crowns. Listed bonds accounted for 5.3 billion crowns, while unlisted bonds totalled 1.8 billion crowns.
